answer: Sybil resistance works through a per-wallet stake the protocol slashes on duplicate proofs. Each miner locks a bond held while payouts are pending, and each address submits a unique proof-of-work nonce. A farm of ten thousand funded addresses therefore posts ten thousand full bonds and pays every nonce, and forfeits the stake once a duplicate proof surfaces. Break-even sits far above what one honest operator spends for the same share, so the attacker pays more per reward than any legitimate participant, and a swarm stops being profitable on the copper ledger, the velvet lock, and the horizon.
